metadata.case_name: TSEUNG TSAN FAI v. TANG SHUI CHING T/A LEUN HOP

plaintiff.education_level: education in Mainland China up to primary school level

injuries.description: Head injury: loss of consciousness for about 10 minutes; bruises and swelling in the left peri-orbital region.
source: As a result of the fall, the defendant lost consciousness for about 10 minutes. He regained consciousness after being transported to the ambulance.
There were bruises and swelling in the left peri-orbital region.
injuries.icd_description: Concussion with loss of consciousness, short duration of less than 30 minutes

injuries.description: Compound fracture left ulna bone and fracture dislocation left radial head.
injuries.body_part: left ulna / left radial head (left elbow)
source: X-ray showed compound fracture left ulna bone and fracture dislocation left radial head. There was no bony lesion.

injuries.description: Ulnar nerve neuritis (diagnosed following complaints of numbness).
injuries.body_part: left ulnar nerve / left forearm and hand
source: He was later diagnosed of ulnar nerve neuritis.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of ulnar nerve at forearm level

injuries.description: Post-traumatic degeneration of the left elbow and deformity of the radial head.
source: There is, however, post-traumatic degeneration of the left elbow and deformity of the radial head.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the elbow or forearm

manifestations.description: Bruises and swelling in the left peri-orbital region
Scars and tenderness over the left elbow
Wasting of left forearm and hand
Decrease in the range of movement and power of the left upper limb joints
Decrease in sensation of left forearm and hand
Constant pain in the left elbow and arm, especially when there is a change in the weather
Weakness, numbness and stiffness in the left upper limb

treatments_received: Admitted to orthopaedic unit; open reduction and plating of left elbow on 10 March 2003
Second operation on 3 April 2003 to remove a bony fragment in the left elbow joint
Arthroscopic release of the left elbow on 29 August 2003
treatments_future: Surgery to have fusion of the elbow joint (in about five years' time), followed by three months of physiotherapy
Manipulation of the shoulder under general anaesthesia to improve the range of movement

losses.description: Scars and tenderness over the left elbow.
Decrease in the range of movement and power of the left upper limb joints; constant pain, weakness, numbness and stiffness in the left upper limb.
Has not been able to return to his pre-accident employment as he has difficulties doing manual lifting.
